synth_calls.reply:
Glucokinase (GCK) is a key glycolytic enzyme that acts as the pancreatic beta-cell glucose sensor, and mutations in this gene are a well-established cause of maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY), particularly the MODY-2 subtype. The findings retrieved from the knowledge graph and NCBI databases identify the GCK gene [1], its literature entity name Gck [2], multiple ClinVar-listed sequence variants in GCK [8-20], and several clinical trials investigating glucokinase activators and GCK-related diabetes subtypes [3-7]. Together, these records provide a comprehensive picture of the genetic and therapeutic landscape surrounding GCK-associated MODY.

## GCK Gene Identity and Nomenclature

The gene symbol for glucokinase is GCK [1], and the corresponding literature entity name is Gck [2]. These identifiers anchor the subsequent variant and trial records to a single locus. The glucokinase enzyme encoded by GCK phosphorylates glucose in pancreatic beta cells and hepatocytes, serving as the rate-limiting step in glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Loss-of-function mutations in GCK reduce the sensitivity of beta cells to glucose, producing the mild, stable fasting hyperglycemia characteristic of MODY-2.

## ClinVar-Listed GCK Sequence Variants

Multiple sequence variants in GCK have been catalogued in ClinVar, each representing a distinct nucleotide or amino acid change in the NM_000162.5 transcript. The variant ClinVar:1028584 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.415A>T (p.Met139Leu) [8]. The variant ClinVar:1045215 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.762T>G (p.Asn254Lys) [9]. The variant ClinVar:1074406 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.359dup (p.Met121fs) [10]. The variant ClinVar:1077171 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.397T>C (p.Phe133Leu) [11]. The variant ClinVar:1098819 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.1139A>C (p.His380Pro) [12]. The variant ClinVar:1172675 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.82G>A (p.Glu28Lys) [13]. The variant ClinVar:1172895 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.691A>G (p.Asn231Asp) [14]. The variant ClinVar:1172896 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.660C>A (p.Cys220Ter) [15]. The variant ClinVar:1179956 is listed with its source URL at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/1179956 [16]. The variant ClinVar:1187444 is named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.434C>T (p.Pro145Leu) [17]. The variant ClinVar:1188508 is listed with its source URL at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/1188508 [18]. The variant ClinVar:1190030 is listed with its source URL at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/1190030 [19]. The variant ClinVar:1190681 is listed with its source URL at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/1190681 [20].

## Variant Type and Mechanistic Distribution

The retrieved variants span several mechanistic categories relevant to MODY pathogenesis. Missense substitutions such as p.Met139Leu [8], p.Asn254Lys [9], p.Phe133Leu [11], p.His380Pro [12], p.Glu28Lys [13], p.Asn231Asp [14], and p.Pro145Leu [17] alter single amino acid residues distributed across the glucokinase protein, potentially disrupting the enzyme's catalytic activity, allosteric regulation, or structural stability. A frameshift variant, ClinVar:1074406, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.359dup (p.Met121fs) [10], introduces a duplication at codon 359 that shifts the reading frame, likely producing a truncated nonfunctional protein. A nonsense variant, ClinVar:1172896, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.660C>A (p.Cys220Ter) [15], converts codon 220 to a premature stop codon, which is expected to result in a truncated protein lacking critical catalytic or allosteric domains. Four additional ClinVar entries—ClinVar:1179956 [16], ClinVar:1188508 [18], ClinVar:1190030 [19], and ClinVar:1190681 [20]—are listed by their ClinVar source URLs without explicit variant names in the retrieved records, and their specific molecular consequences would require direct consultation of the corresponding ClinVar pages.

## Clinical Trials Related to GCK and Diabetes

Several clinical trials in the retrieved data directly implicate glucokinase as a therapeutic or genetic target in diabetes. The clinical trial named A Study of LY2599506 (Oral Agent Medication: Glucokinase Activator 1) in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus [3] evaluates a glucokinase activator, a pharmacological strategy aimed at enhancing GCK enzymatic activity to improve glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. The clinical trial named Using Pharmacogenetics to Improve Treatment in Early-onset Diabetes [4] incorporates pharmacogenetic approaches to diabetes subtypes that include MODY. The clinical trial named A Study of LY2608204 in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes [5] investigates another compound in the type 2 diabetes therapeutic pipeline. The clinical trial named A Clinical Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetics of Oral ZYGK1 in Healthy Volunteers [6] assesses a glucokinase-targeting agent designated ZYGK1. The clinical trial named The Effect of ß-cell Specific Glucokinase Mutation on Glucose Homeostasis and Insulin Secretion in a MODY-2 Family [7] directly examines the physiological consequences of a beta-cell–specific glucokinase mutation in a family affected by MODY-2, linking the molecular genetics of GCK variants to their clinical metabolic phenotype.

## Clinical Significance for MODY Diagnosis

The collective ClinVar variant catalogue for GCK, encompassing missense, frameshift, and nonsense alterations [8-20], provides the molecular foundation for genetic diagnosis of MODY-2. The presence of both loss-of-function truncating variants such as p.Cys220Ter [15] and p.Met121fs [10], alongside missense substitutions scattered across the protein [8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17], underscores the allelic heterogeneity of GCK-associated MODY. The clinical trial examining beta-cell–specific glucokinase mutations in a MODY-2 family [7] reinforces the genotype-phenotype correlation central to MODY-2 diagnosis and management.

synth_calls.reply:
Glucokinase (GCK) is a critical enzyme in pancreatic beta-cell glucose sensing and hepatic glycolysis, and its disruption by missense, nonsense, and frameshift variants is a well-established molecular cause of maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY). The findings retrieved from the knowledge graph and linked NCBI resources identify the gene symbol GCK [1] and the literature entity name Gck [2], together with thirteen named ClinVar sequence variants, four additional ClinVar records identified by source URL, and five clinical trials that underscore the translational relevance of glucokinase pharmacogenomics. Below, these variants and trials are discussed in mechanistic detail.

## Gene Identity and Nomenclature

The gene of interest carries the symbol GCK [1], and the same locus appears in the retrieved literature under the entity name Gck [2]. These two identifiers represent the same glucokinase-encoding gene, which serves as the central node linking all subsequent variant and trial records to a single molecular target. No additional synonyms beyond GCK [1] and Gck [2] were returned by the search.

## Missense Variants in the GCK Coding Sequence

Multiple missense variants were identified in ClinVar records referencing the NM_000162.5 transcript. The variant ClinVar:1028584, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.415A>T (p.Met139Leu) [8], substitutes a methionine with a leucine at codon 139, a residue within the glucokinase allosteric activator domain whose alteration can shift the enzyme's glucose affinity and contribute to the MODY phenotype. The variant ClinVar:1045215, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.762T>G (p.Asn254Lys) [9], changes an asparagine to a lysine at codon 254, a region implicated in substrate interaction. The variant ClinVar:1077171, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.397T>C (p.Phe133Leu) [11], replaces a phenylalanine with a leucine at codon 133, closely positioned to the c.415 variant and likely affecting the same structural fold. The variant ClinVar:1098819, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.1139A>C (p.His380Pro) [12], introduces a proline at histidine 380, a substitution expected to disrupt local secondary structure near the C-terminal portion of the enzyme. The variant ClinVar:1172675, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.82G>A (p.Glu28Lys) [13], converts a glutamic acid to a lysine at codon 28 in the N-terminal region. The variant ClinVar:1172895, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.691A>G (p.Asn231Asp) [14], substitutes an asparagine with an aspartic acid at codon 231. The variant ClinVar:1187444, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.434C>T (p.Pro145Leu) [17], changes a proline to a leucine at codon 145, another residue in the allosteric activator domain.

## Nonsense and Frameshift Variants

A nonsense variant, ClinVar:1172896, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.660C>A (p.Cys220Ter) [15], introduces a premature termination codon at cysteine 220, predicting a truncated protein lacking the C-terminal catalytic segments essential for kinase activity. A frameshift variant, ClinVar:1074406, named NM_000162.5(GCK):c.359dup (p.Met121fs) [10], arises from a single-nucleotide duplication at codon 121, shifting the reading frame and likely producing a nonfunctional glucokinase through premature termination downstream.

## Additional ClinVar Records Without Variant Names

Four further ClinVar sequence variant records were retrieved with source URLs but without displayed variant names in the findings. The variant ClinVar:1179956 is documented at the source URL https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/1179956 [16]. The variant ClinVar:1188508 is documented at the source URL https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/1188508 [18]. The variant ClinVar:1190030 is documented at the source URL https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/1190030 [19]. The variant ClinVar:1190681 is documented at the source URL https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/1190681 [20]. These records represent additional GCK-associated entries in ClinVar whose specific nucleotide and protein changes were not returned in the current retrieval; each is identifiable by its ClinVar identifier and source URL as cited.

## Clinical Trials Targeting Glucokinase Function

Five clinical trials were retrieved, spanning pharmacogenetic approaches and small-molecule glucokinase activators. The trial named A Study of LY2599506 (Oral Agent Medication: Glucokinase Activator 1) in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus [3] evaluates a direct glucokinase activator in type 2 diabetes. The trial named Using Pharmacogenetics to Improve Treatment in Early-onset Diabetes [4] addresses pharmacogenetic stratification in early-onset diabetes, the clinical category encompassing MODY. The trial named A Study of LY2608204 in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes [5] tests a second glucokinase activator compound. The trial named A Clinical Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetics of Oral ZYGK1 in Healthy Volunteers [6] assesses a further oral glucokinase activator in a first-in-human setting. The trial named The Effect of ß-cell Specific Glucokinase Mutation on Glucose Homeostasis and Insulin Secretion in a MODY-2 Family [7] directly investigates the physiological consequences of a beta-cell-specific glucokinase mutation in a family with MODY-2, the subtype classically caused by GCK variants.

## Mechanistic Synthesis

The retrieved variants cluster across the GCK coding sequence, affecting residues in the N-terminal region (p.Glu28Lys [13]), the allosteric activator domain (p.Met139Leu [8], p.Phe133Leu [11], p.Pro145Leu [17]), the substrate-binding region (p.Asn254Lys [9]), the catalytic core (p.Asn231Asp [14], p.Cys220Ter [15]), and the C-terminal domain (p.His380Pro [12]), alongside a frameshift at codon 121 (p.Met121fs [10]) and four further ClinVar records [16][18][19][20]. Collectively, these alterations are expected to impair glucokinase's role as the pancreatic beta-cell glucose sensor, reducing the efficiency of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and producing the mild, stable fasting hyperglycemia characteristic of GCK-MODY. The concurrent clinical trial evidence [3][4][5][6][7] highlights the translational effort to modulate glucokinase activity pharmacologically and to tailor treatment based on the specific GCK genotype.
